objects.name: Apollo 11 — Lunar Module Eagle Descent Stage
objects.description: The descent stage of Lunar Module Eagle, which carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to Tranquility Base. It served as the launch platform for the ascent stage and remains on the lunar surface.
objects.history: Eagle landed in Mare Tranquillitatis on 20 July 1969. Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21.5 hours on the surface before the ascent stage lifted off on 21 July, leaving the descent stage behind.
objects.significance: Site of the first crewed Moon landing and a protected historical site under NASA's lunar heritage guidance.

sources.provider: NASA History — Human Artifacts on the Moon

objects.name: Apollo 11 — EASEP (Passive Seismometer and Retroreflector)

location.description: Deployed near Lunar Module Eagle at Tranquility Base; individual instrument position is not separately catalogued.

objects.description: The Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP) was the first lunar surface experiment package. It included a passive seismometer and a laser ranging retroreflector, and was a simplified precursor to the ALSEP packages used on later Apollo missions.
objects.history: Deployed during the Apollo 11 EVA on 20 July 1969. The seismometer operated for about three weeks; the retroreflector has supported lunar laser ranging for decades.
objects.significance: First geophysical instrument package deployed by humans on another world.

objects.name: Apollo 11 — Laser Ranging Retroreflector
objects.description: A retroreflector array left at Tranquility Base. Ground-based laser ranging stations still use it to measure the Earth–Moon distance.
objects.history: Deployed by Armstrong and Aldrin in July 1969. Laser ranging measurements have continued for more than five decades.
objects.significance: One of the longest-operating scientific instruments left on the Moon.

objects.name: Apollo 12 — Lunar Module Intrepid Descent Stage
objects.description: The descent stage of Lunar Module Intrepid, which landed in Oceanus Procellarum in November 1969. The crew visited the nearby Surveyor 3 spacecraft.
objects.history: Landed on 19 November 1969. The descent stage remained after the ascent stage returned the crew to orbit and later impacted the Moon.
objects.significance: Demonstrated precision landing and the first crewed visit to a previously landed robotic spacecraft.

objects.name: Apollo 12 — ALSEP Central Station
objects.description: Central station of the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), the geophysical network deployed by the Apollo crews. It collected and relayed data from its experiments until the program ended in 1977.
objects.history: Deployed during the Apollo 12 mission in November 1969 and operated as part of the ALSEP network.
objects.significance: Part of the first long-lived network of geophysical stations on the Moon.

objects.name: Apollo 14 — Lunar Module Antares Descent Stage
objects.description: The descent stage of Lunar Module Antares, which landed in the Fra Mauro formation in February 1971. The crew explored the ejecta of the Imbrium impact.
objects.history: Landed on 5 February 1971. The descent stage remains at the site after the ascent stage departed.
objects.significance: First landing in the lunar highlands, targeting material ejected by the Imbrium basin impact.

objects.name: Surveyor 1
objects.description: Surveyor 1 was the first US spacecraft to make a soft landing on the Moon. It returned images and engineering data from Oceanus Procellarum.
objects.history: Launched 30 May 1966 and landed 2 June 1966. The lander operated until January 1967.
objects.significance: Demonstrated the soft-landing technology needed for Apollo.

objects.description: Surveyor 2 failed during its midcourse correction and impacted the Moon. The catalogue records an estimated impact coordinate.
objects.history: Launched 20 September 1966. A thruster failure during midcourse correction caused the spacecraft to tumble; it impacted the Moon on 23 September 1966.
objects.significance: A documented robotic impact site from the Surveyor program.

objects.history: Landed 20 April 1967. Apollo 12 astronauts Charles Conrad and Alan Bean visited the site in November 1969.
objects.significance: The only robotic spacecraft on the Moon to be visited by humans.

objects.name: Surveyor 5
objects.description: Surveyor 5 landed in Mare Tranquillitatis and analyzed the lunar soil with an alpha-scattering instrument.
objects.history: Launched 8 September 1967 and landed 11 September 1967. It operated through December 1967.
objects.significance: Provided early chemical analysis of the lunar regolith.

objects.name: Surveyor 6
objects.description: Surveyor 6 landed in Sinus Medii and later performed the first controlled liftoff from the Moon, hopping a short distance.
objects.history: Landed 10 November 1967. On 17 November 1967 its engines were fired briefly for a small hop.
objects.significance: First spacecraft to lift off from another celestial body.

objects.name: Ranger 4 — Impact Site
objects.description: Ranger 4 was intended to image the lunar surface but failed before returning data. It impacted the far side of the Moon.
objects.history: Launched 23 April 1962. A failure left the spacecraft without power; it impacted the Moon on 26 April 1962.
objects.significance: The first US spacecraft to reach the Moon, though the mission failed.

objects.name: Ranger 7 — Impact Site
objects.description: Ranger 7 was the first US mission to return close-up images of the Moon, transmitting thousands of frames before impact.
objects.history: Launched 28 July 1964 and impacted the Moon on 31 July 1964 after a successful imaging sequence.
objects.significance: Demonstrated the feasibility of lunar imaging for Apollo site selection.

objects.name: Ranger 8 — Impact Site
objects.description: Ranger 8 returned high-resolution images of the Moon before impacting in Mare Tranquillitatis.
objects.history: Launched 17 February 1965 and impacted on 20 February 1965.
objects.significance: Provided imagery used in planning the Apollo 11 landing region.
